name: Kelvex Transit Ground Crew Night Shift Rig
description: A head-to-toe kit built for Kelvex MagRail ground crews pulling overnight platform maintenance shifts. The jacket is a structured navy synth-canvas shell with a broad safety-orange chevron running diagonally across the chest and back, retro-reflective tape stitched along the cuffs and collar seam, and the Kelvex wordmark embroidered in silver thread above the left breast pocket. Underneath sits a charcoal thermal base layer with a mock-neck collar that folds up against wind off the rail corridors. The trousers are Kelvex-branded heavy-duty stretch twill in navy, with reinforced knee panels, a wide tool loop on the right thigh, and a magnetic-closure cargo pocket that holds standard-issue platform tablets. Boots are a steel-toe mid-height lace-up in matte black with orange contrast stitching and a slip-resistant rubber outsole rated for wet platform grating. A Kelvex-issue hard shell helmet in hi-vis yellow clips to a carabiner loop on the jacket's left hip when not worn. Gloves tuck into the back waistband — insulated synth-leather palms, knit back panels.
functionality: Retro-reflective panels for rail-corridor visibility, reinforced knees for platform crawlwork, magnetic cargo pocket for transit tablets, tool loop for handheld diagnostics, thermal base layer for unheated maintenance tunnels, helmet carabiner loop, insulated grip gloves
what_it_says: This is someone who keeps M88 moving whether anyone sees them or not. The Kelvex branding marks them as company property on shift — reliable, unglamorous, essential. The orange chevron signals hazard proximity without apology. Off-shift, the jacket stays on because it's warm and it's theirs.
manufacturer: Kelvex Transit Systems — issued uniform, supplemented with Ironpass thermal base layer
price_range: Φ180–Φ240 (company-issued; replacement cost out of pocket)
story_hooks: A ground crew worker discovers a structural fault in the rail during a night shift that their supervisor ordered them to log as routine — the Kelvex jacket's embedded shift-ID makes them traceable if they report it officially.
The retro-reflective chevron catches a security camera's light at the wrong moment, placing a worker at a platform where a body was found between the 02:00 and 04:00 maintenance windows.
A veteran crew member's jacket has a small hand-stitched patch over the Kelvex logo — a quiet act of defiance that's gotten others quietly fired.
related_entities: Ringo Heavy Transit MagRail Levitation Transport Network

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian, high-visibility ground crew ensemble projecting authority and safety compliance. The broad safety-orange chevron across navy creates a striking diagonal accent that reads instantly in low light. Silhouette is structured and functional—broad shoulders, tapered at wrists and ankles, with visible tool attachment points. Overall impression: working-class infrastructure maintenance, tier 3 or upper tier 4.
physical_description.fit: Tailored for mobility and layering. The jacket sits slightly oversized through the chest to accommodate thermal base layer and permit arm movement during platform work. Trousers have a relaxed thigh with a tapered calf to allow boot insertion. Compression fit at wrists and collar to seal against wind.
physical_description.primary_material: Navy synth-canvas shell (jacket), charcoal thermal-knit base layer, navy stretch twill reinforced with ballistic weave at high-wear zones (trousers), matte black slip-resistant rubber (boots)
physical_description.texture: Jacket canvas has a tight, uniform weave with stiffness—factory-pressed, retains creases well. Base layer is soft-touch synthetic with subtle ribbing. Trousers show subtle texture variation where reinforcement panels overlap. Boots have aggressive tread pattern, tactile rubber compound.
physical_description.color_scheme: Dominant navy with safety-orange chevron accent (ANSI compliant hi-vis). Charcoal thermal layer visible at neck and cuffs. Hi-vis yellow helmet as detachable accent. Silver thread embroidery (Kelvex wordmark). Orange contrast stitching on boots.
physical_description.closures: Jacket: heavy-duty brass zipper with orange pull tab, magnetic snaps at chest pocket, friction-fit cuff tabs. Trousers: standard waistband button with friction-lock fly, magnetic closure on cargo pocket. Boots: traditional lacing with reinforced eyelets. Glove retention: friction fit into back waistband.
distinctive_features: ANSI-compliant retro-reflective tape stitched along collar seam and cuffs for 24-hour visibility
Diagonal safety-orange chevron spanning chest to back—instantly readable in darkness
Kelvex wordmark embroidered in silver thread (brand assertion, corporate uniform identity)
Tool loop on right thigh designed for platform tablet attachment or magnetic flashlight
Magnetic-closure cargo pocket (quick access, no fumbling in darkness)
Hard-shell yellow helmet with carabiner clip-point on left hip (when not in use)
Steel-toe reinforcement visible as subtle black cap at boot toe
Slip-resistant sole rated for wet rail platform grating (safety-critical feature)
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. The quality is solid and purpose-built, not luxury, but indicates stable institutional employment. Issued uniform signals corporate infrastructure workforce.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearer is MagRail infrastructure labor—overnight ground crew, platform maintenance, safety-critical role. The uniform projects reliability, compliance, and night-shift work culture. Orange and navy are standard across Kelvex Transit globally. Wearing this signals you are essential infrastructure backbone, not desk-bound corpo.
physical_description.condition_typical: Factory-fresh on issue, but quickly shows wear at reinforced panels and knees. Creasing at elbows and thighs from repetitive movement. Scuff marks on boot caps from platform grating contact. Retro-reflective tape remains bright (maintained for safety regulation). Some staining from hydraulic fluid or grease near pocket areas is expected and tolerated.
